segments: A bird taller than a grown adult walked New Zealand's forests for millions of years — and it had no wings at all. Not small wings. None.
Nine species of moa lived only in New Zealand, the largest standing over three metres tall and weighing up to 250 kilograms.
For millions of years, nothing on the ground could hunt them — so evolution simply stopped building the parts used to escape.
Every other flightless bird — ostriches, emus, even penguins — still carries wing bones somewhere in its skeleton. Moa lost them completely. The only birds ever found with none at all.
Then, around 1250, people arrived. Moa were not already dying out — populations were large and healthy right up until that moment.
Hunted for meat, eggs and skins, with nowhere to run and no wings to escape with, every single species was gone within about 150 years.
A defenselessness that took millions of years to evolve — erased in roughly a century.
New Zealand lost its most defenseless giant in about a century. Follow for the next extinction story most people have never heard.

title_card.LINE1: The Only Bird With No Wings

metadata.title: Random But True: The Bird With No Wings At All
metadata.caption:
Moa were giant flightless birds in New Zealand — up to 3 metres tall, and the only birds ever found with absolutely no wings at all, not even vestigial ones.

They were safe for millions of years. Then people arrived, and within about 150 years, every species was gone.

Follow for the next extinction story most people have never heard.
